title: Build-Time vs. Run-Time: Why Dev Tools Fail in Production — Averi Kitsch & Prerna Kakkar, Google
talk_summary: Google engineers describe MCP database tool patterns, splitting build-time (flexible, human-in-loop) from run-time (deterministic, production) tools, and lay out a security model separating user/application/agent identities with parameters bound outside agent control. The core transferable ideas are deterministic pre-written tool actions, read/write tool separation, actionable errors, and simple flat inputs.

takeaways.technique: Deterministic pre-written tool actions instead of agent-generated queries
takeaways.what_they_do: Instead of letting the agent generate arbitrary SQL, they define exact statements in YAML as custom tools with fixed names/descriptions and typed prepared-statement parameters, so the agent only supplies a few validated inputs.
takeaways.evidence_quote: we can define the exact SQL uh statement that will run very reliable. It's a reliable and secure uh SQL query.

takeaways.technique: Separate read vs write tools with auto-approve on reads
takeaways.what_they_do: They split tools into read and write; reads can be auto-approved while writes are routed to a user for confirmation, which also makes tool choice clearer for the agent.
takeaways.evidence_quote: separate read versus write tools. Um by doing this you can automatically approve read tools and but you can also then send write tools uh to the user for um confirmation

takeaways.what_they_do: Rather than returning generic HTTP 4xx errors, tools return errors that tell the agent what went wrong and whether/how to retry, so the agent can self-correct.
takeaways.evidence_quote: if you give the ability to have an error of that can be retrieded the agent can actually take that action

takeaways.what_they_do: They avoid complex nested maps/primitives the agent must construct, using flat structures with simple inputs to raise reliability.
takeaways.evidence_quote: Using flat structure with um with uh simple inputs will really increase your reliability.

takeaways.technique: Bind sensitive parameters outside agent control (bounded/authenticated params)
takeaways.what_they_do: PII like user ID is never exposed to the agent; the application authenticates the user and binds the parameter, or the tool validates a signed JWT and extracts claims itself.

takeaways.technique: Outcome-oriented tools, not atomic REST wrappers
takeaways.what_they_do: Tools should perform the whole action needed rather than mirroring atomic REST endpoints, cutting round trips; descriptions give guidance without duplicating parameter info.
takeaways.evidence_quote: tools focus on outcomes. We really shouldn't be thinking in atomic rest APIs. we should think about what the action actually needs to do
